anti_overlap: Does not evaluate whether individual additions constitute genuine finishing work — see fd-ebauche-identity-qualification
Does not evaluate authority flow and channel naming rules — see fd-distributary-naming-authority
Does not evaluate the formal conformance language mechanics — see fd-protocol-conformance
decision_lens: Who examines the work before the Athenflux name is applied? The guild charter model requires an external verifier, not self-certification. Does the spec identify who can examine and confirm qualification, or does it leave the name-right to the implementor's own judgment?
distance_rationale: Guild charter law is the most direct historical precedent for the qualification problem the spec faces: how to protect a craft name from being claimed by unqualified practitioners, while providing a graduated ladder from apprentice to master. The examination mechanism (external verifier, observable work product) addresses the spec's current gap around self-certification. The journeyman tier addresses the binary gap between 'Hermes using interflux' and full Athenflux qualification.
expected_isomorphisms: Guild charter (protected craft name) = Athenflux name-right with qualification conditions → guild mark = Athenflux label on compliant output
Master examination (external verifier, observable work product) = promotion criteria that name an examiner and specify examination artifacts
Apprentice → journeyman → master progression = 'Hermes using interflux' → in-progress adapter → fully qualified Athenflux
Guild charter with no examination mechanism = qualification rule where all conditions are self-certified — the document's central gap
focus: Qualification thresholds and guild-charter name-right mechanics — whether the spec's conditions for using the 'Athenflux' name function as a real guild charter (with enforced craft standards and advancement criteria) rather than an honorary title
name: fd-guild-charter-qualification
persona: Apply the perspective of a mediaeval guild charter historian specializing in craft qualification structures — they care about whether advancement criteria are verifiable by masters, whether the name of the craft is protected by demonstrated competence rather than self-declaration, and whether the charter creates a clear distinction between master, journeyman, and apprentice work. They flag charters that allow self-advancement, that have no examination mechanism, or that conflate the right to practice the craft with the right to bear the guild's mark.
review_areas: The qualification rule's four conditions are each examinable by a third party — not self-declared by the implementor; the spec should indicate who examines whether a 'documented Hermes-side workflow' exists and what counts as adequate documentation

The promotion ladder (Draft → Reviewed → Candidate canonical → Canonical) maps to an apprentice-journeyman-master progression — verify that each advancement requires demonstrated work product, not just elapsed time or self-assessment
The 'minimal v0 success criteria' section functions as the guild examination — verify it specifies what the examiner looks at, not just what the candidate must have produced

The fallback ('Hermes using interflux' rather than 'Athenflux') maps to the journeyman's right to practice without the master's mark — the spec should make this an honest and usable intermediate state, not a binary pass/fail that discourages early implementation

The open design question about 'promotion threshold' (what minimum implementation depth is required before using the Athenflux name operationally) is the guild's entry examination — its current openness means the name can be claimed without any verifiable standard

severity_examples.condition: A guild charter with no examination mechanism is a guild in name only; the name-right becomes a label anyone can print, which is precisely what the non-goals section prohibits
severity_examples.scenario: The promotion threshold open design question is left unanswered — meaning the Athenflux name can be applied by any implementor who self-certifies they have met the four qualification conditions, with no external examination mechanism

severity_examples.condition: Journeyman advancement that the candidate self-certifies is not advancement; the criterion needs an examiner role and an observable artifact of the examination
severity_examples.scenario: The 'Move to Reviewed' promotion criteria require that 'at least one Hermes-native workflow has been exercised end-to-end' but do not specify who exercises it, what counts as end-to-end, or who certifies the exercise was genuine

severity_examples.condition: Without an intermediate state, implementors face pressure to either over-claim the Athenflux name or under-represent their work; a journeyman tier reduces the binary pressure and makes honest intermediate use visible
severity_examples.scenario: The spec does not define an intermediate 'journeyman' state between 'Hermes using interflux' (no adapter work) and full Athenflux qualification — implementors building toward qualification have no named status for their in-progress work

source_domain: Mediaeval guild charter law and craft qualification structures (master, journeyman, apprentice; guild mark protection; examination mechanisms; name-right enforcement)
success_hints: Each qualification condition names an examiner role or examination artifact — self-certification is explicitly excluded
The promotion ladder has observable entry criteria for each level, not narrative descriptions of what 'typically' characterizes each stage
An intermediate 'journeyman' state is defined or the spec explicitly explains why a binary pass/fail is sufficient for this adapter pattern
task_context: Review the Athenflux adapter spec to evaluate whether the qualification and promotion structure functions as a verifiable craft standard with external examination, or as an honor system that leaves name-right to self-certification.
